Hi Marta — thanks for the draft. Quick responses and a proposed 'liquidity clock' we can operationalize: 

1) Tranches: we are amenable to two tranches (50/50) or one full upfront invoice. Two-tranche flow we typically use: 60% upfront at contract signature, 40% at service activation (first production use).

2) Drawdown/sweep triggers (proposed):
   - T0 (signature): invoice 1 released, funds received into Redwood custody account.
   - T1 (activation or 30 days after T0): invoice 2 released and swept to ledger when activation evidence received.
   - Exceptions window: if activation delayed >60 days, we allow a 30-day extension before automatic sweep.

3) VAT evidence: for reverse-charge in the UK we need a VAT registration number and the country-level certificate plus a remittance affidavit for our records. For NL/DE similar — the certificates in your zip look good but our finance team may ask for scanned signed copies for DE.

I've attached a short mutual action plan (MAP) PDF that maps the gating events to required documents and who signs off. If you prefer monthly automated drawdowns rather than tranche release, we can support that via a sweep schedule but it will require explicit ledger tagging.

Can Laura (cc'd) confirm the exact evidence artifacts and whether escrow vs Redwood-custody account changes any VAT handling? Vivek, flag anything I missed on sales terms.

Best,
Ethan Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Ethan / Vivek — adding Finance perspective: 

- Preferred flow: Redwood-custody (standard) for committed spend gives us the cleanest ledger treatment and avoids customer escrow fees. If customer insists on escrow we can accommodate but need the escrow account details and an SLA for release.
- VAT: for UK reverse-charge we need: customer VAT ID (validated against VIES), a signed remit affidavit (one-time), and the invoice must include the reverse-charge notation. For DE we require customer-signed VAT evidence (PDF) and proof of business address.
- Docs: ask customer for a billing contact + AP email for automated remittance. Once we have those we will: 1) produce invoice 1 (60%) immediately on signature; 2) hold invoice 2 as 'pending activation' and tag it in our ledger for automatic sweep when activation evidence posted.

Operational items for MAP:
- Activation evidence = production API key issued + short smoke test (two sample calls).
- AP acceptance: preferred ACH / SEPA instructions; wire accepted but add beneficiary validation lead time.

I'll draft a short checklist (what we need from Halogen) and link to DocuSign placeholders for signatures.

—Laura
